subject: Post-call: pricing & batching follow-up / token volumes + continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T14:00:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes, budget & batching assumptions

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of convo: Acme Health is evaluating using LLMs for triage + patient messaging. You have a pilot scope (clinical triage) with expected growth over 12 months. The team cares most about predictable unit economics, latency SLOs (~<1s tail for triage), and PHI handling (we'll follow up separately on security).

2) Asks I mentioned on the call (can you confirm):
- Expected monthly token volume for pilot and steady-state (best guess: low, target, upside).
- Budget range for inference (monthly) and target $/1M tokens you’d consider acceptable.
- Workload pattern: percent of short (<300 token) requests vs long (>1,000 token) requests, typical QPS (steady vs peak), and concurrency expectations.

3) Why I ask: Our cost and recommended plan depend heavily on batching & concurrency assumptions. For workloads with high QPS of short requests, our continuous-batching runtime can reduce unit costs substantially vs naive per-request pricing. If your traffic is spiky with low concurrency, savings are smaller.

4) Next steps: If you can reply with the bullet items above, I’ll: (a) share an illustrative unit-econ calc for Hosted vs Dedicated with continuous-batching assumptions, (b) attach a pricing sheet and a proposed 3-month pilot plan we can run under a PO.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (pricing bands + commitment tiers).

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes, budget & batching assumptions

Camila — thanks, useful recap. Some answers below based on our internal estimates:

- Pilot volume (first 3 months): ~50M tokens / month (mostly outbound messages + short triage prompts).
- Steady state (12-month target): ~450M tokens/month if we roll out to 3 additional regions; upside scenario ~1.2B tokens/month within 18 months.
- Budget: initial pilot budget is ~$12k/month (we know it's tight for LLMs). For expansion, we can consider $50k-$120k/month depending on unit economics and SLA. Our procurement team prefers seeing a target $/1M tokens to evaluate ROI — ideally <$1,200 per 1M tokens, target closer to $900/1M for long-term pricing.
- Workload pattern: ~85% short requests (prompt+response combined <300 tokens), 15% longer inference for multi-turn triage (~300-1,200 tokens). Peak concurrency during morning triage windows: up to 220 concurrent requests for a short period (5-10 minutes), steady-state concurrency ~40 typical. Average request tokens ~120. Response latency expectation: median <300ms, p95 <1s for triage-critical flows.

Attached procurement form (acme-procurement-req.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick follow-up with Aditya if you need more traffic detail or to confirm commitment tiers.

Alex Johnson | Head of Digital Product, Acme Health
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com | +1 617-555-0110
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes, budget & batching assumptions

Alex — really helpful, thanks for the numbers and procurement doc. I put together an illustrative unit-econ summary and continuous-batching assumptions below (high level) so you can see how we map your target pricing to specific configurations. If this looks good I’ll convert into the pricing sheet and pilot PO language.

Illustrative unit economics (examples — final pricing depends on commitment & SLA):
- Hosted (on-demand) baseline list: ~$1,600 per 1M tokens (no commitment) — this is our public-hosted list for the model family you described.
- Committed Dedicated (3-12 month): can get to ~$900-1,100 per 1M tokens depending on commit and concurrency profile.
- Pilot/discounted band: for a 3-month pilot (200M tokens committed) — we can offer ~$800-950 per 1M tokens plus pilot credits for proof-of-value.

How batching & concurrency drive these numbers (our assumptions mapped to your traffic):
- Your profile: 85% short requests, avg tokens ~120/request, steady concurrency ~40, short peaks to 220 for ~10m windows.
- Continuous batching behavior: for short, high-QPS workloads our runtime continuously aggregates inflight requests into micro-batches (window typically 5-20ms) and also uses prefix caching where applicable. With steady concurrency 40 and short average tokens, we typically observe an effective batching factor of ~1.8-2.5 on this workload (i.e., hardware sees 1.8-2.5x more tokens-per-invocation throughput than naive single-request execution).
- Effective cost impact: with continuous batching & prefix caching, per-1M-token compute cost can drop ~30-40% vs single-request baseline. That’s why a $1,600 baseline can map to $900-1,100 effective per-1M in committed settings.

Key configuration notes & recommendations:
1) Pilot: recommended 3-month pilot w/ 200M tokens committed on a Dedicated pool sized for your AM peak (supporting sustained concurrency ~250). This gives predictable perf and lets us tune batch-window and autoscale thresholds.
2) Autoscaling & burst: keep burst headroom for the 10-min morning spikes; set autoscale to add nodes if avg batch factor drops below 1.4 during peak.
3) SLOs: to hit p95 <1s we expect to serve most short requests from continuous-batching paths plus KV/prefix caching for repeated phrasing. If you need p50 <300ms consistently, we should discuss a mixed routing policy (hot-path reserved nodes).
4) Measurement: we’ll instrument token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, and a continuous-batching factor metric so you can see real savings during pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll update redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx with the pilot band ($800-950 per 1M) and a model of expected monthly bill under the batching assumptions you provided.
- Aditya (cc) will draft the pilot PO + SLA language; we can include a 30% pilot credit if we agree on the scope below.

Does that range and approach look reasonable to you? If yes I’ll send the formal pilot proposal and a short SOW.

Thanks — Camila
